newsitem.title: USA: Michael Foods sees crop improvements.
newsitem.headline: Michael Foods sees crop improvements.

text.p: Michael Foods Inc said on Thursday the problems it faced because of high corn and soybean prices and poor quality potatoes peaked in third quarter.
"We're in the new crop which looks better than last year," said Mark Witmer, a spokesman for Michael Foods.
Michael Foods earlier reported third quarter earnings of $0.07 a share versus $0.22 last year.
The company said the price of feed, mainly corn and soybeans, was 70 percent higher than last year, resulting in what the company called a "significant earnings decline" in its egg products division.
Results in the eggs division, however, were better than expected because of strong sales of eggs products, it said.

"Sales of dried egg products and specialty frozen patties and omelets were particularly strong in the quarter, which helped mitigate the raw material cost pressures," said Gregg Ostrander, chief executive of Michael Foods.

The company said the potato products division operated at a loss due to expensive potatoes and decreased production yields as a result of small or oddly shaped potatoes. Sales in the frozen category were disappointing, it said.
In addition, Michael Foods said it expects its acquisition of Papetti's Hygrade Egg Products Inc to be completed in the fourth quarter.

A shareholders meeting to vote on the pending merger with North Star Universal Inc is also due in the fourth quarter. The company said assuming necessary rulings, the merger is expected to be completed in the first quarter of 1997.
